questions.question: What kind of form is Jordan normal form compared with diagonal form?
options: A form that applies only to nonsquare matrices.
An almost diagonal form built from Jordan blocks.
A diagonal form with no possible off-diagonal entries.
A row echelon form obtained by elementary row operations.

questions.question: What matrix relation expresses the Jordan normal form of A?
What are the diagonal entries of Jordan normal form?
options: Entries of the right-hand side vector.

questions.question: If A is diagonalizable, what does its Jordan normal form look like?
options: It has only zero diagonal entries.
It has one large Jordan block for every eigenvalue.

questions.question: What objects are used to build Jordan normal form when ordinary eigenvectors are not enough?
Is $\begin{pmatrix}2&1\\0&2\end{pmatrix}$ already in Jordan normal form?
options: No, because the diagonal entries are equal.
Yes, it is a single Jordan block.
Only if the determinant is zero.
No, because it is not diagonal.

questions.question: Is the diagonal matrix $\operatorname{diag}(1,3)$ in Jordan normal form?
options: Only if one diagonal entry is zero.
No, because the eigenvalues are distinct.
Yes, a diagonal matrix is already in Jordan normal form.
No, because Jordan normal form must have a 1 above the diagonal.

questions.question: For $J=\begin{pmatrix}4&1\\0&4\end{pmatrix}$, which eigenvalue appears on the diagonal?
Which matrix could be a Jordan normal form with one block of size 2 for λ=5?
If a Jordan normal form has diagonal entries $2,2,3$, what are its eigenvalues with algebraic multiplicity?
What feature distinguishes a non-diagonal Jordan form from a diagonal form?
options: The diagonal entries are not eigenvalues.
The matrix has no block structure.

questions.question: Why is Jordan normal form useful for defective matrices?
options: It still gives a structured form using generalized eigenvectors.
It turns defective matrices into diagonalizable matrices.
It avoids any change of basis.
It removes all eigenvalues from the matrix.

questions.question: Does the equation $J_A=P^{-1}AP$ mean A and $J_A$ represent the same linear operator in different bases?
options: Only if P is the identity matrix.
No, $J_A$ is obtained by row reduction.

questions.question: If A is diagonalizable with eigenvalues 1 and 4, which Jordan form is consistent?
A Jordan form has blocks $J_2(3)$ and $J_1(5)$. What is its size?
For $J=\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\0&2&0\\0&0&5\end{pmatrix}$, what are the Jordan block sizes?
options: One block of size 2 for 5 and one block of size 1 for 2.
One block of size 2 for 2 and one block of size 1 for 5.

questions.question: When is Jordan normal form exactly diagonal rather than merely almost diagonal?
options: When there is exactly one eigenvalue.
When all Jordan blocks have size 1.
When every block has size at least 2.

questions.question: Why do Jordan block sizes contain more information than just the eigenvalue list?
options: They replace the determinant by the trace, under all circumstances whatsoever.
They list the entries of P directly.
They determine the field of scalars.
They record how eigenvectors and generalized eigenvectors are arranged.

questions.question: A $4\times4$ matrix has Jordan form $J_3(0)\oplus J_1(0)$. How many Jordan blocks appear for eigenvalue 0?
A Jordan form consists of two $1\times1$ blocks for λ=2 and one $2\times2$ block for λ=2. What is the algebraic multiplicity of 2?
